back: Compares the target with the middle item of a sorted list and discards the half that cannot contain it; repeats until found or Low > High.
Mid ← DIV(Low + High, 2). If Data[Mid] < Target then Low ← Mid + 1, else High ← Mid - 1.
The list must be sorted; the loop ends when the item is found or Low > High (not found).
⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1 comparisons: 4 for 12 items, 10 for 1 000, 20 for 1 000 000.
Takes each item in turn and inserts it into its place among the earlier, sorted items by shifting larger items right.
The item being inserted is saved in Key because the first shift overwrites its place.

front: Insertion sort best and worst case
back: Best: already sorted, n − 1 comparisons, no shifts. Worst: reverse order, n(n − 1)/2 comparisons and shifts.
Linear: unsorted, short or one-off. Binary: sorted, long or searched many times, with direct access to items.

front: Not found in a binary search
back: Low becomes greater than High, so no items remain; Found is still FALSE.
